findings.title: getForLogin cache does not honor organization invalidations, unlike getByOrganization
findings.body: In getForLogin, the only staleness check is `isInvalid(cacheKey)` on the realm+mode login key. The analogous cached query method getByOrganization (line 173) additionally checks `isInvalid(orgId)` because organization-level changes (org update, org removal, IDP link/unlink performed through the organization APIs) register invalidations under the organization id, not under IDP cache keys. Any IDP link/unlink or org removal that does not route through IdentityProviderStorageProvider.update() (and therefore never triggers registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate) will leave the cached getForLogin lists stale: e.g. after an organization is removed its formerly-linked IDPs become realm-level login IDPs, but the cached REALM_ONLY list will not contain them and the ORG_ONLY/ALL lists may still reference them, until some unrelated IDP change happens to invalidate the login keys. The method should also consult the organization invalidation (or register login-cache invalidation from the organization provider) before serving cached results.

findings.title: Cleanup registers removal of literal alias "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
findings.body: In testCacheIDPForLogin the cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove)` — the literal string "alias" rather than the loop variable `alias`/"idp-alias-" + i. The same mistake exists for idp-alias-20 (line 425). As a result none of the 21 identity providers created by this test are actually cleaned up (the lookup for alias "alias" finds nothing), leaking IDPs into the shared test realm and potentially affecting other tests that run afterwards in the same class/suite.
